INTERVIEW WITH PHAINON — OKHEMA DAILY NEWS

I: Phainon! It’s good to see you around again! How have you been?

PHAINON: I’ve been great!

I: How’s retirement treating you?

PHAINON: Oh, it’s been amazing. Went back home after many years, and I’ve been resting a lot. I even picked up some new hobbies which are really fun. It feels like a weight has been lifted off my shoulders, not saying that MotoGP is a burden, of course. Don’t get me wrong, I love MotoGP, and the people, and all of the supporters. But it’s a different feeling back home when I’m just Khaslana, a boy born in a small village, not Phainon, this guy, the MotoGP Legend as the people call him, surrounded by people full of expectations of him every year to win another title. No expectations, no pressures. I feel human again. 

I: That’s great to hear! I’m sure your fans will understand. You haven’t made any appearances since almost half a year ago! Any reason for that?

PHAINON: Well. To put it simply, I had to step away. It may sound cliche but I had some soul searching to do, as Cyrene would say. MotoGP and motorsports in general had been a large part of my life. I’ve been on some type of vehicle longer than I have not. I just had to take the time to get to know myself again, who I am without MotoGP, so to speak. And to do that, I had to completely remove myself from the picture, lest I start missing the chaos and adrenaline again. [Laughs] 

I: And we all know how much of a big fan you are of Formula One. Were you sad that you weren’t around for the first couple of rounds?

PHAINON: Oh, definitely. Once, I was on a call with Mydei and I was whining about being sad that I wasn’t able to support him in person, especially with such a rough start of the season for him, so he spent 15 minutes comforting me and assured me that it was fine. I’m very grateful to have him. 

I: I’m sure he feels the same, too.

Breaking Free: Phainon reflects on his career in MotoGP

Welt Yang

Astral Express

It’s the year of 4064, and somewhere in a small village called Aedes Elysiae, a baby’s cry rang aloud. The elders celebrate at the birth of a new life. At the time, nobody knew that little babe would grow to become a prominent figure in motorsports history. 

At age 5, Phainon reached out for an electric mini bike. He instantly fell in love with it and dreams to become the best motorcycle racer that Amphoreus has ever seen. Out of love and support, his parents sent him to Castrum Kremnos where the finest racers are being groomed, where his idol, Gnaeus, hailed from. It was a huge investment for a couple that made their living as farmers. But it turned out well, didn’t it?

Phainon had always been an exceptional rider. Before entering the premier class, he had already caught the attention of multiple race team managers while competing in Moto3 and Moto2. They claimed that Phainon has ‘unimaginable raw talent’ that no one has ever seen before. One team manager had said, “Phainon, that boy, he is destined for greatness.” 

[Photo: Phainon in his race leathers, holding his helmet and his eyes closed.]

Then, his promotion to MotoGP arrived. Long time fans of the sport were skeptical. Phainon had spent only 1 year in each class. Some fans expressed it was too soon, that Phainon was too young and should stay in Moto2 for at least another year before moving up to where the big guys play. Some fans argued that the Venerationist Racing Team were making a huge mistake in taking Phainon. Time and time again, Phainon proved them all wrong. In the first race, he achieved his maiden win and broke the record of the youngest rider to win. Against all odds, he won his first title in the premier class. 

 

In a forum that’s been long shut down, this quote emerged which hit the headlines quickly:

 

“Phainon’s dominance in his rookie year wasn’t him proving everyone wrong, it was a warning.”

 

“I remember when my manager showed me that quote,” Phainon tells Astral Express, “I laughed so hard seeing it. I thought it was ridiculous. Warning? It clicked to me then how dramatic the sport could be.”

 

15 years on, Phainon proved to be a fierce competitor. It was a dominance that no one has ever seen before. 4091, 4094, 4095. Those were the only years that Phainon did not manage to snag the championship title for himself. 4091, due to his injury-induced hiatus. 4094 and 4095, due to regulation changes and Nousporist were struggling to be competitive. And yet, Phainon managed to seat himself in P2 in the Rider Standings for both years, so close in points behind the leader—just like a predator breathing down the neck of its prey. 

 

Then, to everyone’s surprise, Phainon announced his retirement after winning his 12th title.

 

“The short answer? I was burnt out,” he says. “The long answer… I felt as if I was losing myself. Amidst the wins and the prestige, I find myself weary and just wishing to rest. At some point, I felt like I was just a well oiled machine, coming to the paddock to win a trophy and then going back home to recover for that short period in between races, and the cycle repeats.”

 

[Photo: Phainon on the podium, holding his trophy up with his hands and grinning.]

 

“It was mentally tiring, too. Too many mind games with the pundits,” he says while laughing bitterly, “On a good day, they sing praises and have these high expectations of me to always do something amazing and win the races and perform for the world. On other days, they get mad at me for winning all the races and not giving any chances to the other riders to win, especially the newer guys. When I don’t win, they say that I’ve lost my spark. It’s like, what the fuck do they even want from me?” 

 

After three consecutive years where a MotoGP world champion announced their retirement during Phainon’s reign, the name Flame Reaver was born. It was the media’s last ditch attempt to break a young Phainon’s mental integrity. Athletes having nicknames and titles given by the masses weren’t new, in fact, it was considered an honour to receive one; it means that you’ve made it, that you have become an athlete of a calibre. 

 

To Phainon, however, it wasn’t an honour. It was a challenge. He started as the hero, the Deliverer, when he brought the Nousporist Racing Team to victory. As Flame Reaver, he promised to become the villain that the media claimed him to be.

 

“At first I thought it was a cool name, then it was just a bitter feeling. Was it so wrong that I wanted to win? All of us wanted to become racers with the intention to win, to be the best of the best. It’s a competition, a survival of the fittest, but when I’m the only one winning, it’s wrong?” 

 

Of course not. Whether to infuriate those who made him the villain or to play along with his new nickname, Phainon raced harder than before, leaving no margins of error that his rivals could take advantage of, and intimidating his peers on and off track. 

 

Castrum Kremnos, 4097. Phainon was back in his residence at Castrum Kremnos when he started toying with the idea of retirement. He had just won the race and instead of celebrating, he chose to spend time alone in his apartment.

 

“It was like a lightbulb moment,” he says with a laugh. “I’ve never really thought about retirement so when the thought came, I thought to myself, ‘am I ready for that?’ because retirement was a big step to take. All my life, I’ve only ever known racing, I never had a backup plan if my MotoGP career went to shit. So the thought was just brewing in my mind for a while.”

 

Then, it was a season break, and for the first time in a long time, he returned to Aedes Elysiae.

 

“The first thing that stood out to me was the tranquility. Watching my parents tend to the fields despite their age with their friends, seeing the children run around and play with each other. It occurred to me then just how much I missed home.”

 

Phainon laid on his childhood bed, he closed his eyes, and his mind was made.

 

“I knew then what I needed to do. The thought of retirement had been at the back of my mind and refusing to leave. So I made a deal with myself, just to get my twelfth title as a fun challenge. I thought it was fun, having twelve titles while racing with the number twelve.”

 

“That year was arguably one of the most important years of my career, because I knew I was going to leave everything behind once the season wraps up. I was set on leaving on high spirits and having fun. I wanted to leave while I still felt love for the sport, if you know what I mean. The funniest part is I didn’t even tell anyone. Not my friends, not my family. I did talk to my partner [Mydeimos, partner of Phainon, 3-time Formula 1 World Champion] about it here and there but I’ve never told him when. I really was just surprising the entire world!”

 

[Photo: Group photo of Phainon and Nousporist Racing Team at Phainon’s last race.]

 

Going out with a bang. That was Phainon’s motto for the year.

 

“I had a lot of fear and doubts, of course. ‘Am I making the right call?’ or ‘is it too soon?’ or the question that plagued my mind the most: ‘and then, what?’.”

 

And then, he took time to get to know himself outside of racing. He spent his first few months in Aedes Elysiae relearning how to tend the field from his parents. Then, he picked up books on antique appraisals. His newfound love for antiques gave him a new set of challenges that allowed him to focus and not think about racing. To top it all off, he began a warrior’s training regimen. Yes, including sparring. 

 

“I wanted a way to keep my body fit and my mind sharp… it just so happens my partner is Kremnoan and I’ve lived in Castrum Kremnos for basically more than half my life, it felt fitting that I train like a Kremnoan warrior from the past.”

 

Back home in Aedes Elysiae where Phainon now resides, he slowly reacquaints himself with the little joys that the world offers. His brain has permanently switched off from race mode. He begins his day like this: a light exercise to wake his body and mind up, followed by a relaxing bath to soothe his muscles. Then, he helps out in the fields or the livestock farm. Depending on the day, he’ll look at antique wares for his collection and practise appraisal, or hit the gym again for a proper spar with his personal trainer. And the activity that he looks forward to the most: a call in the evening with his partner. 

 

“He is one of the most important people in my life. He’s my anchor when I feel like everything is too overwhelming. He’s someone I know I could trust with every worry in my body because deep down, he understands what it feels like,” he explains. “It’s funny because back then, I never believed in soulmates or any of that romantic stuff. After meeting Mydeimos, though, it was like every single atom in my body was screaming ‘that person, he’s our soulmate!’ and I just knew. Whether or not soulmates exist, I have already acknowledged that Mydeimos is the only one worthy to be my equal.”

 

[Photo: Phainon and Mydeimos walking together in the paddock.]

 

Until today, hopeful fans are still waiting for Phainon to make a comeback into the motorsports world no matter which race series. His choice? It’s clear as day—he will enjoy his hard earned retirement in his home where he can finally be himself.

 

“I will always love MotoGP. That is an undeniable fact. I’ve built my career in MotoGP and loved it my entire life. Maybe sometimes they don’t love me back, but that’s okay! For now though, I am at peace with the ending I’ve chosen.”

chapters.html:
End Notes

i've uhm and ahh'd about phaidei's wedding attire for a long time but chose their in-game outfits in the end because it fits them so well and u cannot change my mind !!

i like to imagine that mydei loves to cuddle up to phainon's neck where his sun tattoo would be because
1) i like to compare mydei to the sun sometimes so ofc he'd be where phainon's sun tattoo would sit !
2) i hc that phainon's body runs warm all the time and mydei loves the warmth (he's like a cat)

mydei calls phainon by his different names depending on his mood lmao
- phainon being his typical everyday name
- khaslana when its intimate or talking about something serious
- deliverer when he's not happy with phainon

hephaestion and phainon's relationship didnt mean to happen actually i wasnt planning on them to be besties but it just happened and im like oh okay! and i've seen people hc that hephaestion is mydei's ex etc in their own fics or ideas and i find it so funny and adopted it.

i really wished we knew more about the kremnoan culture,, cultures in general is one of my favourite topics to dive into and i really wanted to expand more on it but i dont think a social media au is apt for it LMAO hopefully in another fic! initially i wanted mydei to present a sword to phainon as a kremnoan wedding tradition but,,, idk. i think it'd be cool especially bc they were a military nation in history.

phainon's mental struggle is something i wish i was able to expand more on but i didn't want to take away the lightheartedness of a social media au. but he was also somewhat inspired by one of my own favourite retired f1 driver on top of his in-game lore,, being a fan of both motogp and f1 and being in the fandom for a while now, witnessing the riders/drivers' obvious struggles is one of the worst things to have happened to me and i may have projected my feelings here (oops)

also i kinda made references to the in-game lore and all but it's not to signify reincarnation or anything, it's more of like their souls are so intertwined with each other that they see visions of their alternate universe selves (and unfortunately for u phainon, its more suffering.)

this is the end of this universe unfortunately. i hope you loved them as much as i do :)
